- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.4) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 3–5 days.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.4), model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% for next 3–5 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (≥ 3% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +2% above peak for next 5 days.  
- Model consistently underestimates mean-reversion periods (e.g., after 78–80 range); add 0.5–1.5% upward bias for 3–7 day horizon.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating +/– swings (e.g., +0.36, -1.25, +0.43), model fails to capture momentum; adjust forecast to align with sentiment direction over 3-day window.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often misses late-period corrections; add 0.5–1.0% upward bias if sentiment turns positive after day 15–20.
